production.note: US model years. First: "The 2005 Scion tC" "will go on sale nationally in late June 2004" (scion-2005-tc-pricing). Last: "Following a successful first-generation model, Scion introduces the all-new 2011 Scion tC sports coupe", which "first launched in 2004" (toyota-2011-tc-release), so the first generation ended with the 2010 model year.

body.note: Liftback sport coupe (the brochure "redefines the sports coupe"); liftbacks count as coupes.

aspiration.note: Inferred: the brochure describes a 2.4-liter four with no turbocharger or supercharger (a TRD supercharger was a dealer accessory, not a factory rating).

fuel.note: Inferred from the brochure's description of a conventional piston engine.

transmission.note: "Transmission 5-Speed Manual (Standard)"; "4-Speed Automatic (Available)". Same pairing at launch: "five-speed manual transmission model" and "four-speed electronically controlled automatic transmission" (scion-2005-tc-pricing).

powerHp.note: 2009 model year. Quote: "Horsepower 161 hp @ 6,000 rpm". Early cars were rated 160 hp: Scion's April 2004 pricing release describes "a 160-horsepower engine" (scion-2005-tc-pricing) and Carey Russ's 2005 review lists "160 @ 5700 rpm" (autochannel-2005-tc-review). No opened page states in which model year the published rating changed (the change reflects revised SAE rating practice, not a mechanical change); the 2009 brochure is the only manufacturer document opened (the 2005 brochure is no longer on Auto-Brochures), so the reference year is 2009.

weightLb.note: 2009 model year, 5-speed manual. Quote: "Curb Weight 2,932 lbs. (Manual)" ("2,987 lbs. (Automatic)"). See discrepancies for a different 2005 figure.

sources.publisher: Scion (Toyota Motor Sales, U.S.A.; brochure rehosted by Auto-Brochures.com)

discrepancies.reason: Model year and source class: 2,932 lb is Scion's 2009 brochure figure for the manual; 2,970 lb is from a 2005 press review whose configuration is not stated.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the manufacturer's 2,932 lb for the manual at the 2009 reference year.

reviewNotes: The model year the published rating changed from 160 to 161 hp was not found on an opened page; the 2009 brochure is the only openable manufacturer document, so its 161 hp / 2,932 lb and reference year 2009 are used. If 160 hp in fact covered 2005-2008, the guide's majority rule would prefer that rating.
